doc.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: New York studio guitarists and drummers of the era
summary: He lists the guitarists and drummers on New York studio dates, including Bacharach and Bennett work.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But I’ve done a lot of film dates. In New York when I was — at sort of the tail end of a certain kind of vintage guitar player, there were guys like Tony Mottola and Bucky Pizzarelli, Barry Galbraith, Howie Collins and Al Caiola, Al Cassamentes. And the younger crew like David Spinozza and — oh the guys are going to hate me for forgetting — I worked a lot with a guy named Jay Berliner, Billy — well anyway, Ralph Casales. We were still getting calls for a lot of recordings and film dates. And I did a lot of stuff in the studios. All Burt Bachrach’s work, all of Tony Bennett’s records, and I was always the young guy on the block and I was that for a while. Particularly with drummers. There was a guy that was on every date. I remember a guy named Dennis — well first there was Bobby Rosengarden. When I first came up he was doing all the work. Then a guy named Bill Lavorgna, who started conducting recently for Liza Minelli. Then there was a guy named Dennis Siewell, who was always on every date. And after that, the last big gun,
there was a guy named Donald McDonald for a while. And the guy — oh he’s going to hate me. The guy was from Rochester, he used to play with Chuck—
Steve Gadd was on every date.
